_comment: Candidate local models for start_litellm_proxy.sh's interactive menu, served via mlx_vlm.server (not Ollama — see LITELLM_PROXY_USAGE.md for why). Every entry here has been through verify_max_kv_size.sh with verdict SAFE before being added; do not add a model to this file without running that script first. 'display' fields are shown to the user when picking a model, in plain language they can act on without reading the underlying research docs.

_schema_notes.size_gb: Real on-disk size, measured directly (du -sh on the cached HF repo), not estimated from quantization bit-width.
_schema_notes.max_context_architectural: The model's trained/architectural context ceiling, read from its own config.json (max_position_embeddings). This is NOT the same as a safe operating context on any given machine — see recommended_max_kv_size_gb_tier (pending) once real-load memory testing is done.
_schema_notes.verification: Result of verify_max_kv_size.sh — confirms mlx_vlm.server's --max-kv-size admission gate actually rejects oversized requests for this model rather than silently ignoring them (the failure mode Ollama's MLX runner has, unfixably, per LITELLM_ROUTING_PLAN.md §4.15 and upstream Ollama issue discussion). It does NOT confirm real long-context memory safety — that needs a separate near-cap-fill test (LITELLM_ROUTING_PLAN.md §4.14 methodology) not yet run for any model in this file.
_schema_notes.tool_calling: Whether OpenCode/Claude Code's tool calls (webfetch, bash, edit, etc.) actually come back as a structured, parseable tool_calls response instead of silently degrading to plain chat text. Determined by LIVE testing (real /v1/chat/completions request with a tool schema attached, temperature=0), not by static inspection of the chat template or by which mlx_vlm tool_parser gets auto-assigned — several models (the whole qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct family) get assigned a parser (json_tools) that matches their template's markers, yet still fail live because the model itself doesn't reliably emit the <tool_call> tags its own template instructs it to use. That specific failure was independently reproduced on TWO OTHER serving stacks besides mlx_vlm (vLLM — see github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder/issues/180 — and Ollama/llama.cpp, tested directly on this machine 2026-09-28), confirming it's a property of the model's own fine-tuning, not a bug in any one harness. phi-4-mini-instruct-4bit is the opposite case: Microsoft's own model card documents real function-calling support and benchmarks it on Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard, but mlx_vlm's tool_parsers registry (mlx_vlm/tool_parsers/__init__.py's _TEMPLATE_MARKERS) has no entry matching Phi's <|tool|>/<|tool_call|> token format, so mlx_vlm never even tries to parse its output — a serving-stack gap, not a model capability gap (vLLM has a dedicated --tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json for this exact model, merged via vllm-project/vllm#14886). KNOWN GAP (historical): model_advisor.py did NOT read this field, so the interactive picker would recommend a NOT_SUPPORTED model (e.g. the former qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct or phi-4-mini-instruct-4bit entries, both since removed from this catalog — see PROJECT_STATUS.md items #20-#21) for coding tasks without warning that tool use would silently no-op. Any future NOT_SUPPORTED entry added to this catalog has the same exposure until model_advisor.py is updated to read this field. Same pattern as max_context_verified_safe's documented gap above; fixing both in model_advisor.py at the same time would make sense.

display.good_for: Verifying the local model stack works end to end, and instant replies to trivial one-off questions. Not a real coding assistant — too small to trust with anything you'd actually ship.
usage_examples: "Reply with exactly the word: pong" — smoke-test that opencode/Claude Code → LiteLLM → MLX is wired up correctly before loading a bigger model
"What's the syntax for a Python list comprehension?" — quick trivia lookup, not real code generation
display.known_issues: Too small for real coding work — expect frequent mistakes on anything beyond a trivial snippet. Use only to test the pipeline itself, never as a daily driver.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. Real long-context memory load not stress-tested, but model is small enough this is low risk.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call (name + JSON arguments) on the first attempt, despite being the smallest model in this list (0.6GB) — structural tool-call support is not a function of model size for this family.

display.good_for: The lightest multimodal (vision-capable) option in this list — fills the gap between the tiny text-only models and the 12B+ multimodal models. "E4B" is Gemma's elastic/MatFormer naming (effective ~4B capacity), not a typo for a plain 4B model.
usage_examples: "What does this error dialog screenshot say, and how do I fix it?" — lightweight vision Q&A without the memory cost of the 12B multimodal model
"Summarize this scanned receipt/document image" — small-scale multimodal tasks on a 16-24GB Mac
display.known_issues: 131K architectural ceiling — smaller than the plain 12B/26B Gemma-4 models (262K), since this elastic variant trades some capacity for its smaller footprint. As an elastic/MatFormer model, its internal cache-building path differs from the plain Gemma-4 models — verified separately rather than assumed safe by analogy.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. First elastic/MatFormer-architecture model tested — passed despite having a different cache-building path than the plain gemma-4-12b/26b models, which was worth checking rather than assuming.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call on the first attempt.

display.tagline: Lighter version of our trusted 12B multimodal model
display.good_for: Same model as gemma-4-12b-it-8bit already in this list (proven safe), just 4-bit instead of 8-bit — meaningfully lighter (6.31GB vs 12GB) for a 16-24GB Mac that still wants vision support.
usage_examples: "What's wrong with this UI based on the screenshot?" — visual analysis, same capability as the 8-bit version
"Describe the architecture shown in this diagram" — vision+text reasoning with more memory headroom left over
display.known_issues: Same thermal/efficiency caveat as the 8-bit sibling (Gemma-4's architecture is less MLX-efficient at long context than Qwen3.5's). 4-bit quantization trades some accuracy for the smaller footprint versus the 8-bit version.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call on the first attempt.

display.good_for: The strongest general recommendation once you have 24GB+ of RAM — a real 128K-class context window with the fastest measured MLX throughput of any model in this list (1.7-2.5x faster than its own GGUF counterpart at every context size tested, per prior benchmarking).
usage_examples: "Work through this repo-wide refactor" — tasks that need the model to hold a lot of file context at once
"Let's pair-program through implementing this feature over several turns" — long multi-turn sessions without hitting context limits quickly
display.known_issues: 9.7GB of weights alone is too much on a 16GB Mac — leaves too little headroom for KV cache plus the OS and background apps. Not recommended below 24GB.

verification.notes: First model verified — admission gate confirmed at 32/256/1024-token bounds, matching upstream mlx-vlm PR #1995's own reproduction scale exactly (that PR reports this class of model silently ignoring max-kv-size on 97/173 mlx-vlm-supported models; this specific model was not one of them, at least for single-turn HTTP requests).

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached (multi-turn round-trip tested: initial call + tool result fed back + final answer). Independently re-confirmed via Ollama 0.33.2 (qwen3.5:9b) through its OpenAI-compat endpoint.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls on both mlx_vlm and Ollama, and correctly produced a coherent final answer after being fed a fabricated tool result in a second request. The most thoroughly-tested working model in this list.

display.tagline: Best all-around choice on 16GB+ Macs (lighter quant of our 8-bit favorite)
display.good_for: Same real 128K-class context window and family strengths as qwen3.5-9b-mlx-8bit, at 6.3GB instead of 9.7GB — fits meaningfully tighter memory budgets (16-24GB Macs) while keeping the same architecture and measured strong MLX throughput advantage over its GGUF counterpart.
usage_examples: "Work through this repo-wide refactor" — tasks that need the model to hold a lot of file context at once
"Let's pair-program through implementing this feature over several turns" — long multi-turn sessions without hitting context limits quickly
display.known_issues: 4-bit quantization trades some accuracy for the smaller footprint versus the 8-bit sibling — expect it to be a notch behind qwen3.5-9b-mlx-8bit in output quality when memory allows using that instead.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds via verify_max_kv_size.sh — correctly rejected oversized requests (HTTP 400) at every scale tested, and correctly recalled a planted secret at the high bound. Real long-context memory load not yet stress-tested (same open gap as most other entries in this file).

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call (name + JSON arguments) on the first attempt. Same architecture/tool_parser as the 8-bit sibling (qwen3.5-9b-mlx-8bit), which was also multi-turn-verified; this 4-bit build was tested single-turn only.

display.good_for: Tasks that need image understanding, not just text — the smaller of the two multimodal candidates in this list.
usage_examples: "What's wrong with this UI based on the screenshot?" — visual analysis of an image
"Describe the architecture shown in this diagram" — vision+text reasoning
display.known_issues: Prior benchmarking found Gemma-4's architecture is thermally less efficient on MLX than Qwen3.5's hybrid attention — expect earlier fan/thermal escalation at long context than qwen3.5-9b-mlx-8bit. Not viable on 16GB.

models._active_weight_note: MoE (num_experts=128 per config.json), but config.json is missing num_experts_per_tok — cannot compute the active-expert fraction the way qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct-4bit's config allowed. Left null deliberately rather than guessed; model_advisor.py's speed estimator correctly reports 'unknown' for this model rather than a fabricated number. Needs its own live decode-speed benchmark to get a real active_weight_gb.

display.good_for: More demanding vision+text tasks than the 12B model can handle well — the larger of the two multimodal candidates.
usage_examples: "Analyze this multi-page scanned document and extract the key data" — larger-scale multimodal document analysis
"Compare these two screenshots and describe what changed" — more demanding vision reasoning
display.known_issues: Same thermal caveat as the 12B sibling, at a larger scale. Not viable on 16GB or 24GB Macs — this is a 32GB+ recommendation only.
